summary: Site of lookout structures since 1915, the present 1958 R-6 tower was last regularly staffed in 1988 and is now a seasonal Kootenai NF rental.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on 41-foot treated timber tower

staffing.status: regular staffing ended 1988; occasional staffing recorded in 1995, 1998, 2000; now primarily a rental

access.note: Primitive, high-clearance roads to a gate on Forest Road 4407, then 5.3 miles to the lookout; gated road also open to hikers.

visit.trail_note: Road 4407 is closed to motorized use except for lookout guests; open to hikers.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest

events.note: 50-foot pole tower with L-6 cab and separate log cabin living quarters built in the 1930s.
Present 41-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab built.
Last year of regular staffing per NHLR; occasional staffing recorded in 1995, 1998, and 2000.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, January 3, 2015.

evidence.quote: then a 45' pole platform in 1915, a frame cupola cabin about 1919, and a 50' pole tower with L-6 cab along with log cabin living quarters in the 1930's. The present 41' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab was built in 1958

evidence.supports: staffing history, 1988 last regular, 1995/1998/2000 occasional, rental program
evidence.quote: Last regularly staffed in 1988. But was staffed in 1995, 1998, and 2000 also. Beginning this year it is on the rental program. No Osborne firefinder in the LO, but it could still be staffed sporadically, and probably will be.

evidence.supports: used for fire spotting since 1958, rental season, facilities, road access
evidence.quote: The lookout tower has been used as an observation point for spotting forest fires since 1958.
Yaak Mountain Lookout road 4407 is gated, use the combination provided. Follow road 4407 for 5.3 miles to the lookout.
The lookout sits atop a 45-foot tower and has a catwalk encircling the cabin.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives the present (1958) tower as 41 feet; Recreation.gov's facilities section calls it a 45-foot tower. Story states the 41-foot figure (from the construction-specific source) once and avoids repeating a conflicting number elsewhere; height_m corrected to match the 41-foot figure.

notes_for_editor: NHLR comment ('Beginning this year it is on the rental program') is undated in the scraped text; story avoids asserting a specific rental-start year. The brief's 1958 built date matches both sources. Fact-check 2026-10-04: story repeated both a '41-foot' and a '45-foot' figure for the same present-day tower (firelookout.com vs Recreation.gov); removed the duplicate conflicting number from the amenities sentence and corrected facts.height_m (was 15.2m, matching the 1930s 50-foot tower, not the present 41-foot one) to 12.5m.
